name: 311. DeepSeek native Messages passes through to the Anthropic-compatible endpoint (TXE-6548) (deepseek-native-messages)
description: Fork contract (TXE-6548, Bifrost-Tokun contract C2, C5, C11): DeepSeek implements AnthropicMessagesEndpoint ({base}/anthropic), so POST /anthropic/v1/messages with a deepseek/ model takes the byte-preserving native passthrough to https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages instead of the Responses bridge, which dropped every Anthropic field the Responses structure has no slot for. Only the model value changes (the provider prefix comes off, and a key alias becomes its model id); DeepSeek's status, headers and body come back unchanged, including its Anthropic-shape usage. The routed-identity header x-bifrost-request-type names the path (passthrough, passthrough_stream). Because the body is no longer rewritten, a named tool_choice now reaches DeepSeek with thinking at its default (on), and DeepSeek answers 400 (api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api); the fourth case pins that the 400 is DeepSeek's own. The third case goes through the harness profile's deepseek-v4-flash-anthropic key alias: core resolves aliases per key, and the shared Messages client now swaps the alias name in the body for its model id. The unary, stream and alias cases also pin x-bifrost-routing-info-server-side-fallback-model: DeepSeek serves deepseek-v4-flash as deepseek-flash and echoes the requested id, so the datasheet's server_side_model is stamped for pricing on this path as on the bridge. Byte-exactness is pinned offline by TestAnthropicMessagesRouteDeepSeekForwardsBodyByteExact in transports/bifrost-http/integrations. Run with FEATURE=deepseek-native-messages. Cases 1-4 need the live DeepSeek API (thinking-mode refusal, real answers) and skip when providerErrorFixture=1. Cases 5-8 run offline against tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs with the gateway of tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json (providerErrorFixture=1): the fixture plays DeepSeek's Anthropic endpoint under /pp/oc/anthropic, records the bytes it receives (GET /__wire), and its datasheet serves fx-deepseek-flash as fx-deepseek-served; each row finds its own request by a metadata.user_id marker, so no fixture reset is needed.

item.name: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash /anthropic/v1/messages takes the native passthrough and returns DeepSeek's usage - TXE-6548

exec: // Needs the live DeepSeek API: the fixture rows below pin the same wire behaviour offline.
if (pm.variables.get('providerErrorFixture') === '1') {
pm.execution.skipRequest();
var txt = pm.response.text();
pm.test('deepseek native Messages: 200 from the native passthrough (TXE-6548)', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + txt.slice(0, 400)).to.eql(200);
pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('x-bifrost-request-type'), 'took the Responses bridge, not the native passthrough: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.eql('passthrough');
pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('x-bifrost-provider'), 'answered by another provider').to.eql('deepseek');
pm.test('deepseek native Messages: body is DeepSeek\'s Anthropic message, unchanged', function () {
var j = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(j.type, txt.slice(0, 300)).to.eql('message');
pm.expect(j, 'Bifrost wrapped the vendor body: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.not.have.property('extra_fields');
var text = (j.content || []).filter(function (b) { return b.type === 'text'; }).map(function (b) { return b.text; }).join('');
pm.expect(text, 'no text block: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.include('391');
pm.test('deepseek native Messages: Anthropic-shape usage as DeepSeek sent it (C5)', function () {
var u = pm.response.json().usage || {};
pm.expect(u.input_tokens, 'input_tokens: ' + JSON.stringify(u)).to.be.a('number');
pm.expect(u.output_tokens, 'output_tokens: ' + JSON.stringify(u)).to.be.a('number').and.above(0);
pm.expect(u, 'OpenAI-shape usage means the body was converted: ' + JSON.stringify(u)).to.not.have.property('prompt_tokens');
if ('cache_read_input_tokens' in u) pm.expect(u.cache_read_input_tokens).to.be.a('number');
pm.test('deepseek native Messages: the served model is stamped for pricing, as on the bridge (TXE-6548)', function () {
// DeepSeek serves deepseek-v4-flash as deepseek-flash and its Anthropic endpoint echoes the requested id,
// so the datasheet's server_side_model is the only source; the native body is the vendor's, so only the header carries it.
pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('x-bifrost-routing-info-server-side-fallback-model'), 'served model not stamped on the native path').to.eql('deepseek-flash');
